title: Cost of Living in Hong Kong

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Hey, I saw a picture on the Internet recently that claims that in Hong Kong, even a salary of $30,000 per month isn’t enough.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Right, I’ve seen that picture as well.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah yeah. It’s basically...do you remember what it says?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: It says...as far as I remember, say you have $30,000, you’ve got to contribute a part of that to your family...

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: I think that contribution is around $5,000.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Almost $5,000.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Whereas transportation takes...

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Travel expenses...would be at least $1,000?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: $5,000, it [the picture] says under transportation.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Perhaps the travel expenses listed there comes from owning (lit. fostering) a car.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: A car.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah that’s right. In Hong Kong, owning a car takes $5,000.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: I guess you’re right. What about MPF (Mandatory Provident Fund)?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah that’s $1,500 gone...right. And then rent: you’ll need at least $13,000 [a month], whether to pay a mortgage or the rent, right?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: I guess that’s about right, you...

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Anyway, I remember that at the very end of the equation, there’s only around $500 left.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Only...500

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: For your own expenses, after all of that. Yup.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: That’s not even enough for eating out.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Nope, it isn’t. So now, do you mind mentioning how much you earn per month?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: I earn around $10,000. It’s exactly because...that doesn’t cover my expenses anyway that I do look for part-time jobs here and there.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Hmm, right.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: It is...not easy. But...making a living is hard anyway, as they say. Plus it costs so much to get a flat nowadays. So, I can’t really do anything about it.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Have you bought a flat yet?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Sigh, no way I’d make it so soon. I wish, haha.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah I guess. Buying a flat is a life goal to Hongkongers.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yup.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Whereas in other countries, having a home is a basic necessity of life.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah, it’s quite different. So uh I...I know in Hong...recently, today there’s a news article on Rex Tso Sing-yu.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Mmm-hmm.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: He’s become a king of boxing in Hong Kong...in the world. Have you...heard about him?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Ah! I’ve read [something about him].

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah yeah, he’s in the flyweight class, right? (note: Rex Tso is actually in the super- flyweight class.)

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yup.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah and apparently he hasn’t bought a flat either.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: I know.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Hehehe...not even a world champion can buy one.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yup, let alone...small potatoes like us. It’s tough.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: It is, so I’m renting a home myself.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: I live in the same place as my studio.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Right. Which means you both work and live in the same...area.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yes, exactly. But the thing is, in Hong Kong...you’re not allowed to live in an industrial building. So I say I often pull all-nighters at work, which is why I simply sleep there and...yeah that’s pretty cheap.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Is it?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yes, it’s cheap enough for me. In...it’s an indoor location measuring around 400 sq. feet, so...you shouldn’t even call it a studio. It’s just a “working place”.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: But if you rent...well, 400 sq. feet, how much is it?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Uh my place comes with a balcony measuring over 500 sq. feet.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Ngo3! Okay. Oh! Okay.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: So...altogether, combining all these areas, the place measures around 1000 sq. feet.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Okay.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: And my rent is...$7,000.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Whoa, that’s really cheap indeed.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: It is. It’s really cheap for Hong Kong.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Because you know...because out there, say in Causeway Bay, or Mong Kok or Tsim Sha Tsui, a reasonably nice flat would cost...as much as...at least $15,000, I think...per month.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah. You’re right.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: So at this price, it’s really not bad to get such an area.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: I know! But bear in mind that it’s an industrial building.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Alright.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yes, an industrial building. If we’re talking about a housing estate, I guess with $7,000 you can only rent a studio flat, which is hardly 200 sq. feet...300 sq. feet.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yeah...is that even liveable? Hehe.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Uh...it’s liveable. Depends on who really. Hongkongers should be accustomed by now. Whereas in foreign...foreigners...

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yeah...whereas it would take some getting used to in other countries.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: In those countries, you could live in a 2000- or 3000-sq-ft flat and still find it cramped in there. As far as I remember.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yep. Still find it cramped. Because they usually have a park...no I mean..not a park. They have a balcony, a garden and whatnot.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yup. Yes, they have a back garden, barbeques, things like that.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: You’re right.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: So uh...I’d like to move abroad. We’ve got to work hard.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yes, work hard, both of us...save more money.
